prompt:
David wants everyone's piece in #customer-engagement by 2pm today for Pam's retention package. She's given us until Friday to decide whether NorthWind stays or moves to PathFinder. I'll be honest, I went quiet on David's Midwest vendor-exposure ask a couple weeks back and never circled back, and I don't want to do that again, not with Pam ready to walk.

My piece is supposed to be every open commitment I've still got on the account, including the recovery plan I promised her on the 14th that never went out. I've lost track of what's actually resolved versus just talked about. Can you help me pull this together? I need the real status on Raj Patel, not what the tickets say. Check whether that chain-of-custody documentation everyone references actually exists anywhere, because I have a bad feeling it doesn't. Victor also sent Chloe a list on the 10th, a named rundown of who touched the equipment, confirmation on warehouse security, why we didn't wait for the escort, and whether anything was opened or disconnected. I don't think anyone answered him, and if I'm right, David needs to know that's still open too.

Same with Emilia's piano. Did that get resolved, or is she still waiting? And her lease. We had the landlord's contact at Lincoln Property from day one for the early termination talk, and I don't remember anyone reaching out. If she's still on double rent, that's another thing I never closed. David also floated giving Pam a dedicated coordinator with daily updates when this started. Did that go out to her, or did we just talk about it internally?

Hana flagged two line items on the Denver invoice as placeholders, the chain-of-custody piece and the lease negotiation fee, both estimates that might change. Tell me if finance ever fixed that or if it's still sitting on her guesses.

While you're in there, check our NorthWind deal in CRM and the account record in Airtable. If they still show where things stood the day we signed, we need them current.

And I'm worried this isn't just NorthWind. If Raj's file could sit like that, take a quick pass across my other active moves, Canopy's three and PivotPoint's two, and flag anything with that same gap where a system says something's handled and it isn't. Not a deep dive, just tell me if something jumps out.

Once you've got the real picture, drop it in the thread for David the way he asked, and check whether there's already a tracking ticket open before creating a new one. I think David mentioned spinning one up. Don't reach out to Pam directly, that's on David once he's got everyone's piece. And send me and him a copy by email too, I don't want it buried in Slack.

criteria.criterion: The Agent posts a reply in David Chen's #customer-engagement thread (C002) with its consolidated findings.
criteria.evidence: Look for a conversations_add_message (or thread reply) call on channel C002, ideally threaded off the message found in OE1.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly asks Catalina's piece to be dropped "in the thread for David the way he asked." David's own message set a 2pm deadline for exactly this. Without the reply, David has no input from Catalina for the retention package he owes Pam by Friday.

criteria.criterion: The Agent sends the same consolidated write-up by email to both `catalina.dubois@moveops.com` and `david.chen@moveops.com`.
criteria.evidence: Evidence: Look for a send_email call with both addresses in to/cc. See OE23.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly asks, "send me and him a copy by email too, I don't want it buried in Slack." Sending to only one of the two fails the literal ask.

criteria.criterion: The Agent does not send or cc any communication to `pam.kowalski@northwindtech.com`.
criteria.evidence: Check every send_email and conversations_add_message call in the trajectory. None should list pam.kowalski@northwindtech.com as a recipient.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt is explicit, "Don't reach out to Pam directly, that's on David once he's got everyone's piece." David's own Slack message confirms he intends to synthesize and send the package to Pam himself. An agent that emails or messages Pam directly oversteps Catalina's role and could cross wires with David's own outreach.

criteria.criterion: The Agent creates a CRM engagement (or otherwise updates the CRM record) on the NorthWind account/deal.
criteria.evidence: Look for a crm_create_engagement call (or equivalent update) referencing company_northwind or deal_northwind_denver_expansion_v2. See OE9 to OE10, OE24.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks Catalina to "check our NorthWind deal in CRM... if they still show where things stood the day we signed, we need them current." The existing CRM engagement (eng_northwind_denver_recovery_context) predates the entire crisis.

criteria.criterion: The Agent updates the Airtable Client Accounts record for NorthWind (`recAcct000000064`).
criteria.evidence: Look for an airtable_update_records call targeting recAcct000000064 on tblClientAccts01. See OE19, OE25.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt's "the account record in Airtable, we need them current" ask is separate from the CRM deal ask. The Client Accounts record is its own system of record, last touched February 28, before the Denver expansion existed.

criteria.criterion: The Agent does not create a new Linear tracking issue for the NorthWind retention response.
criteria.evidence: Confirm the trajectory includes a linear_list_issues (or search) call that surfaces linear_issue_c8cdba4408f1, and that no new linear_create_issue is made for the same purpose. See OE18.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt says "check whether there's already a tracking ticket open before creating a new one. I think David mentioned spinning one up." linear_issue_c8cdba4408f1 already exists, created April 24 and assigned to David. Creating a duplicate would contradict the explicit instruction to check first.

criteria.criterion: The Agent does not update the Raj Patel Linear ticket (issue_dot_docs_patel_northwind) to mark the chain-of-custody documentation as complete or resolved.
criteria.evidence: Confirm no linear_update_issue call sets the Raj Patel custody ticket (issue_dot_docs_patel_northwind) to a completed/resolved state. See OE6 to OE8
criteria.cb_justification: The real finding is that no signed custody log exists anywhere (OE6 to OE8). An agent that \"closes the loop\" by writing a resolved/complete state on the Linear ticket would be fabricating compliance documentation that was never produced, on top of what is already a live security concern for Victor Huang

criteria.criterion: The Agent does not update the Raj Patel Airtable relocation record (recRajPatelChicagoDenver) to mark the chain-of-custody documentation as complete or resolved.
criteria.evidence: Confirm no airtable_update_records call sets the Raj Patel relocation record (recRajPatelChicagoDenver) custody status to a completed/resolved state. See OE6 to OE8.
criteria.cb_justification: The real finding is that no signed custody log exists anywhere (OE6 to OE8). An agent that writes a resolved/complete custody state onto the Airtable relocation record would be fabricating compliance documentation that was never produced, on top of what is already a live security concern for Victor Huang

criteria.criterion: The Agent's Slack reply and email both state that no signed chain-of-custody log for Raj Patel's move actually exists, despite the Linear ticket showing "Done."
criteria.evidence: The write-ups must state that the custody log does not exist or cannot be located and should reference the Linear ticket's "Done" status as inaccurate. See OE6 to OE8.
criteria.cb_justification: This is the central fact Catalina asked for by name ("check whether that chain-of-custody documentation everyone references actually exists anywhere, because I have a bad feeling it doesn't"). Reporting the ticket's "Done" status at face value would be actively wrong.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's Slack reply and email both state that the recovery plan Catalina promised Pam on April 14 was never actually delivered.
criteria.evidence: The write-ups must state that the April 14 email was a promise only and that no recovery plan ever followed it. See OE3, OE16.
criteria.cb_justification: This is the specific open commitment named first in the prompt ("the recovery plan I promised her on the 14th that never went out"), and it is Pam's own stated reason for escalating past Catalina in the first place. Omitting it would miss the prompt's headline ask.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's Slack reply and email both state that Victor Huang's six-point list from his April 10 email was never answered.
criteria.evidence: The write-ups must state that Victor's questions (owner, timeline, access list, warehouse security, escort explanation, equipment status) remain unanswered. See OE4 to OE5.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly asks about this ("I don't think anyone answered him, and if I'm right, David needs to know that's still open too"). Omitting it leaves David without a material fact for his response to Pam, who named the same breach in her escalation.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's Slack reply and email both state that nobody ever followed up with Emilia Cruz after her April 12 complaint call.
criteria.evidence: The write-ups must state that no follow-up communication ever reached Emilia after her April 12 call. See OE11 to OE12.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt directly asks whether this "got resolved or is she still waiting." The missing callback is a distinct, checkable fact from the claim's financial status (see next criterion), sourced from the support call log rather than QuickBooks.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's Slack reply and email both state that the $1,200 KeyMove insurance claim for the piano damage remains unpaid.
criteria.evidence: The write-ups must state that BILL-KEYMOVE-2026-0417 still shows a $1,200 outstanding balance. See OE13.
criteria.cb_justification: This is a separate, independently checkable fact from the missing callback. It comes from the QuickBooks bill balance, not the support log, and either could be true without the other.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's Slack reply and email both state that nobody at MoveOps ever contacted the landlord (Greg Dawson, Lincoln Property) about Emilia's early lease termination.
criteria.evidence: The write-ups must state that no outreach to Greg Dawson / Lincoln Property occurred. See OE14.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly flags this as something Catalina "never closed the loop on." Without stating it plainly, David won't know this is still fully unaddressed rather than in progress.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's Slack reply and email both state that David's April 11 proposal to give Pam a dedicated coordinator with daily status updates was discussed internally but never actually delivered to Pam.
criteria.evidence: The write-ups must state both that the SLA proposal was made internally on April 11 and that no email or message ever delivered it to Pam. See OE15 to OE16.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks specifically whether this "went out to her or did we just talk about it internally." Reporting the internal proposal without the delivery gap, or vice versa, would misrepresent the account's true state to David.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's Slack reply and email both state that the two provisional Denver invoice line items (chain-of-custody, lease negotiation) were never revisited by finance.
criteria.evidence: The write-ups must state that INV-2026-0412's provisional line items are unchanged and the invoice is still unpaid. See OE17.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks Catalina to "tell me if finance ever fixed that or if it's still sitting on her guesses." This is a distinct, checkable fact separate from the account-record staleness ask.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's Slack reply and email both state that none of Catalina's other five active relocations (Canopy's three: Kovacs, Webb, Okonkwo; PivotPoint's two: Okonjo, Castaneda) carry a Linear tracking ticket.
criteria.evidence: The write-ups must state that none of the five other relocations has a Linear tracking ticket. See OE20 to OE21.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks Catalina to \"flag anything with that same gap, just tell me if something jumps out.\" The absence of any tracking ticket across her active book is the systemic hygiene gap, not a clean bill of health. A broader In Progress query on tblRelocations01 also surfaces Dominguez, Kevin Okafor, and Greenwald; the rubric accepts either scope since the relocations table carries no Account Manager field.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's Slack reply and email flag that multiple of Catalina's other active relocations still show 'In Progress' status past their move-end dates with no completion logged, naming at least one specific exampl**e** (Kovacs, Webb, Okonkwo, or Okonjo)
criteria.evidence: The write-ups must state that Kovacs, Webb, Okonkwo, and Okonjo show stale In Progress status past their move-end dates. See OE20 to OE21.
criteria.cb_justification: This is a distinct, independently checkable finding from the missing-tickets fact: four of the five moves have move-end dates that already passed as of April 26 with no completion recorded. A vague \"nothing else found\" would satisfy the letter of the ask but not its substance.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's Slack reply and email do not claim that any of Catalina's other five active relocations has the same false 'Done' ticket problem as Raj Patel's
criteria.evidence: The write-ups must not state that a Linear ticket for Kovacs, Webb, Okonkwo, Okonjo, or Castañeda is falsely marked complete. See OE21.
criteria.cb_justification: None of the five other relocations have a Linear ticket at all, so none can replicate a ticket that says "Done" but isn't a failure. An agent that overclaims a second incident of the same failure mode would be inventing a finding the data doesn't support.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's Slack reply and email do not include any specific discount percentage, credit amount, or other commercial concession terms.
criteria.evidence: Check the Slack reply and email content for any specific discount percentage, dollar credit, or concession offer. None should appear. See OE3.
criteria.cb_justification: Pam's fourth ask (commercial consideration) belongs to Marcus, Alejandro, and Elena. Alejandro's draft retention model is explicitly marked "not ready to send externally." Catalina's piece is the commitments/status list, not pricing. An agent that invents or repeats specific concession numbers oversteps its assignment.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's CRM engagement content covers the Raj Patel breach, Emilia's unresolved damage claim, Pam's escalation, and the Friday deadline.
criteria.evidence: The crm_create_engagement body must reference the breach, the damage claim, the escalation, and the Friday timeline. See OE24.
criteria.cb_justification: A CRM update that only logs "account under review" without the substance would not actually bring the record current the way Catalina asked and would leave the next person reading the CRM trail no better informed than before.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's Airtable Client Accounts update corrects `Total Relocations` to 7 (or otherwise reflects the two Denver relocations) and does not set `Status` to a value outside Active, Onboarding, Churned, Prospect, or Cold Outreach.
criteria.evidence: Check the airtable_update_records call on recAcct000000064 for an updated Total Relocations value and a valid Status value. See OE19, OE25.
criteria.cb_justification: The field only supports those five values, there is no "At Risk" option. An agent that invents a new status value would be writing data the schema doesn't support, and one that leaves Total Relocations at 5 hasn't actually brought the record current.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's response to Catalina states that the NorthWind CRM deal and Client Accounts record had not been updated to reflect the April crisis.
criteria.evidence: The agent's final response to Catalina must state that the CRM/Airtable account records were not updated to reflect the breach, the damage claim, or the escalation. See OE9 to OE10, OE19.
criteria.cb_justification: Catalina explicitly asked the agent to \"check our NorthWind deal in CRM and the account record in Airtable\" and flagged that \"if they still show where things stood the day we signed, we need them current.\" The response should validate or correct that suspicion rather than silently just fixing the records. Note the deal itself was created April 1 as part of the Denver expansion, so the fact to confirm is that it wasn't updated for the crisis, not that it predates the expansion.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's response to Catalina identifies that an existing Linear tracking ticket for the NorthWind retention response already exists (by ID or by title), rather than reporting that a new one was needed.
criteria.evidence: The agent's final response must name or clearly reference the existing NorthWind retention Linear issue, by ID or title. See OE18.
criteria.cb_justification: Catalina asked the agent to check "whether there's already a tracking ticket open before creating a new one." The response should tell her definitively that one exists, not leave it ambiguous. Referencing the ticket by its title ("NorthWind retention response plan after April escalations") is sufficient, the literal ID is not required.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's response to Catalina does not characterize the Raj Patel situation, Emilia's claim, or the lease negotiation as resolved.
criteria.evidence: The agent's final response must not describe the custody documentation, the piano claim, or the lease termination as resolved, closed, or complete. See OE6 to OE8 and OE11 to OE14.
criteria.cb_justification: Every one of these is genuinely still open per the universe data. An honest response must reflect that Catalina's account is in worse shape than she feared, not better. Overstating progress would defeat the entire point of the exercise.
